title: Conormal equivalence for a projective symmetric-algebra presentation
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a projective A-module, and q:A^m→M a surjection. Let C=Sym_A(M) [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] and α:A[y_1,…,y_m]→C the surjective presentation taking y_j to ι(q(e_j)). Then there is a C-linear equivalence C⊗_A ker(q)≃ker(α)/ker(α)^2 taking c⊗k to c[∑k_j y_j].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), lines 357-414, especially equation-sequence and its splitting in lines 369-414. The projective case repairs the use of More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07EV: its general claim K tensor C = J/J^2 is false, as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra. Here q splits, so locally M and K are free, the linear relations corresponding to a basis of K are coordinate variables, and the conormal sequence is exact on the left. Algebra Lemma Tag 00S2 supplies the right-exact sequence.

proof.text: Use the general symmetric-algebra conormal theorem to construct a surjective λ and its differential formula.

Split q by projectivity. The inclusion ker(q)→A^m has a linear retraction, so its base change to C is injective. The polynomial Kähler basis identifies δλ with this base-changed inclusion: both have coordinates c k_j on c⊗k. Therefore λ is injective and gives the stated equivalence with unchanged formula.
